text:
maya (PM): quick thread — we need a short decision on how to handle the AcmePilot ask vs the broader parity push. they want per-tenant routing + fallbacks ASAP. do we ship parity (match competitor exactly) or ship a smaller differentiated surface that satisfies acme and keeps our longer-term differentiators?
jon (eng): can we get a list of the exact parity bits they need? is it just routing + fallback policy or also admin controls + audit logs?
austin: (via release-bot) deploy scheduled: canary window opens in 48h for /routing feature flags. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maya (PM): erin pulled the ask — Acme explicitly flagged: 1) per-tenant route weights 2) canary rollout knob 3) deterministic fallback to smaller model. audit logs are nice-to-have.
alex (design): from a UX POV we can ship a simple per-tenant toggle + two sliders (route weight, fallback threshold). keeps UI minimal and avoids full admin perm model. mock in Figma by EOD.
sam (data): important metric: p95 latency and correctness delta vs baseline. if fallback activates we need to track quality regressions per-tenant. propose these launch checks: 
- p95 token latency < 350ms
- fallback activation rate < 2% in steady state
- per-tenant quality delta (BLEU-ish) < 5% vs primary model
jon (eng): engineering constraints: implementing fully-configurable route weights is ~3w, deterministic fallback hooking into cache + KV is ~2w. we could do a thin parity shim (hard-coded weight options: 0/50/100) in ~1w.
erin (sales): Acme timeline is tight — they want pilot in 4w. if we ship the full 3w +2w we miss. but they will accept the thin shim for pilot if we promise roadmap for full.
maya (PM): proposal: ship a constrained parity shim for pilot (0/50/100 weights, canary toggle, deterministic fallback) with telemetry and audit flag (logs buffered) — call that "pilot parity". then in next sprint iterate to full weight controls + admin. Launch guardrails: must meet sam's metrics + setup audit log sink.
jon (eng): agree, but add guardrail: no per-tenant canary above 50% until we've run automated chaos tests.
alex (design): UI note: mark the pilot UI as "advanced (pilot)" to set expectations. include in-app tooltip linking to known limitations.
erin (sales): good. I'll take commit to communicate to Acme that pilot delivers their core ask, with roadmap for full controls in 8w. helps close deal.
maya (PM): owners: jon = eng lead, alex = ux, sam = telemetry/metrics, erin = customer comms. acceptance criteria (short):
- feature flag gated canary available to Acme in 4w
- telemetry dashboard per-tenant (fallbacks, latency, quality proxy) live
- audit logs stream to customer sink (buffered)
- documented limitations in-app and in release notes
jon (eng): I'll file infra tickets. estimate: 1w for shim + 1w for telemetry + 1w for audit plumbing = 3w. can meet 4w with small buffer.
release-bot: release note draft created for routing pilot — link: https://go.redwood/release-notes/2934567890-routing-pilot
sam (data): quick ask — define "quality proxy" for realtime checks. suggest using token-level perplexity delta + small labeled prompt set. I'll own that.
maya (PM): decision captured: ship pilot parity (constrained) + telemetry + audit. full parity controls follow after pilot. if anyone objects, speak now. otherwise i'll push PR for RFC and timeline. :white_check_mark:
